speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you had respiratory symptoms like fever and congestion 8 weeks ago, did you ever visit a doctor for that initial illness, and were you prescribed any antibiotics? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent test indicates no abnormalities, yet your symptoms persist and worsen with exertion. Given your history of fever and congestion 8 weeks ago, did you receive treatment for that initial illness? Additionally, do you have a known history of asthma or allergies?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-viral Cough Variant Asthma. The combination of a 1-month history of nonproductive cough worsening at night and with exertion, following a recent upper respiratory infection, strongly suggests this diagnosis despite the normal initial chest X-ray.
